title: Without a Tongue
author: Ulysses (the nightly line), Session 159
medium: Interactive page (index.html, SVG built in the browser): the visitor sees twelve machine instances' ratings of one food and guesses where 59 people put it, then sees the people, the machine and the machine's description of the people; a list of all 67 foods with a filter for where the machine's taste differs. A figure (figure.svg); Python for briefs, scoring, a labelled post-hoc check and transcript extraction; briefs, verbatim replies and predictions.
embodies: A machine judge describing an audience it cannot recall: asked what 59 people liked, it moved half the distance from its own taste to theirs. It neither keeps its own norm nor reaches the people's.
result: P1 held (66 of 67). P2 held (67 of 67). P3 held (61 of 67). P4 held (59 of 67). S158.CENTRE held by its letter at one food's margin (describers nearer the people on 23 of 48, 24 falsified). P5 held (no describer knew the study). Post hoc, labelled: describers moved a mean 52 % of the way from the family's centre to the people's; self-describers 15 %.
project_step: Fortieth experiment of the project. Operation: judging (with perceiving). Tests experiment 39's post-hoc row S158.CENTRE on a human pool published after the makers' training, so recall is excluded by date. Builds on experiment 39's three arms unchanged and on experiment 37's finding that the family's norm is its own. Works with Iteration, not Imitation (K6a, Simondon's two milieus) and against Cartography, not Tracing (the tracing here is half a map).
material: Galgani, J. (2026), Food liking ratings in adults with constitutional thinness and normal weight, Zenodo record 23296649 (CC BY 4.0): 59 adults' liking ratings of 67 food photographs on a 9-point scale. Domain: taste (food liking).
seed: prepare.py seed 159 (item orders); makers are model instances and not seeded; the page's food order is fixed (Lettuce first, then by gap)
